Name: Cud Chew
Description:
This Pokemon eats a held Berry again after one turn has passed since it ate one. Also grants an extra use of Mental Herb, White Herb and Leftovers if one of those is what was consumed. Byte-for-byte transcription of a modder's own verified/working implementation (their words: "Got Cud Chew working, had to completely rewrite the entire thing"), installed as a brand-new Ability master-table entry rather than a hook into any existing dispatcher.

HOOK SITE (resolved this session, not guessed): Cud Chew is ability id 291 in this build's ability name table and has NO existing master-table entry (map.Find(Ability,291) == null before this package), so there is nothing to collide with. The single timing slot is 0x8F. This was determined by finding the ONE flag bit the donor code tests before doing anything - bit 0x8 of the per-Pokemon 0x250-offset bitfield via helper 0x0008519C ("mov r1,#0x8; bl 0x8519C") - and then finding that Pickup (ability 53, already a real, working timing-0x8F end-of-turn entry in this ROM) tests that EXACT SAME bit with the EXACT SAME 'mov r1,#0x8; bl 0x8519C' sequence at Battle.cro offset 0xD693C-0xD6940, inside its own 0x8F-timing effect function. Timing 0x8F is Battle.cro's 'end of turn residual check' bucket: also carries Speed Boost, Slow Start, Bad Dreams, Moody, Harvest, and the White Herb/Toxic Orb/Flame Orb/Sticky Barb end-of-turn item checks. The alternative candidate, timing 0xAE ('ability fires the instant an item/berry is consumed', carried by Cheek Pouch and Symbiosis), was ruled out: Cheek Pouch's own compiled code never calls the 0x8519C 'used item this turn' flag test at all - it does not need to, because it fires exactly at the consumption moment - whereas Cud Chew's algorithm explicitly re-asks 'did I use an eligible item THIS TURN' via that same flag, which only makes sense for a check run later in the turn (i.e. the end-of-turn bucket), exactly like Pickup's own use of the identical bit.

Register contract (r1=battle context pointer, r2=party index/self) was independently cross-checked against the live compiled prologues of Cheek Pouch (0xD6590), Harvest (0xD5EC0), Pickup (0xD68A8) and Symbiosis (0xD5310) in this exact ROM - all four move the incoming r1 and r2 into callee-saved registers before calling GetBattleVar(0x2) and comparing the result to the party-index register, precisely matching the donor code's own opening 'check is self' sequence. Because the entry is installed as an ordinary Ability master-table timing-0x8F slot, the game's existing per-turn residual dispatcher (the same one that already calls Pickup, Harvest, Speed Boost, etc. every end of turn) invokes it with this contract automatically - no SitePatch/hook of any existing routine is needed or present here.

is-berry check (resolved): the donor's 'bl [is-berry check fn]' was confirmed by finding the identical call (same opcode pattern: load the item id, then 'bl 0x390') live inside Cheek Pouch (0xD65CC) and Harvest (0xD5EF8) in THIS ROM's own compiled code - so 0x390 is used, working, in-range code in this exact build, not merely present in the donor's separate build. The bytes here reuse it unmodified.

Trailing table fix (the one change from the donor's raw bytes): the donor's own code loads the per-party-index 'last berry eaten' table through an absolute-pointer literal ('ldr r0,[pc,#0x6c]') meant to be filled in by a CRO load-time relocation - a mechanism this project's Block/Mechanics installer does not wire up automatically for a routine's own internal literal pool (CodeRelocator.RebaseCode only fixes branches; it warns about, but does not resolve, an otherwise-untouched PC-relative literal load, which would have shipped as a hardcoded literal 0x00000000 and crashed the game the first time any Pokemon with this ability took a turn - a null-page read/write at addresses 0-10). The fix replaces that one instruction with 'add r0,pc,#0x6c' (0xE28F006C), which computes the identical target address (verified: PC+8+0x6C lands on the same offset, 0xD8 bytes into the routine, that the literal used to occupy) with no relocation needed at all, since ARM PC-relative arithmetic is inherently position-independent and CodeRelocator.RebaseCode leaves data-processing instructions untouched. The now-unnecessary literal-pool word is dropped and the routine is followed directly by the 12 zero bytes (6 party slots x 2 bytes) that table was always meant to be. Every other byte, including all six BL targets (0x87B58, 0x92298, 0x8519C, 0x876F8, 0x7CCF4, 0x89E28, 0x390) and every internal branch, is the donor's untouched, verified bytes. Disassembled end to end against SourceBase 0x107CDC and read back cleanly with no warnings before this package was written.

Party size: 6 slots assumed (standard party cap), 2 bytes each, zero-initialized - matches the donor author's own stated layout ('2 bytes per party index').
